questions.persona: Self-employed tradie off work after an injury, car loan
questions.question: Broke my wrist, can't work for at least 8 weeks and I'm self employed so no sick pay. Car loan repayment due Friday. Can I just pause it for a couple months? Do I need doctor certificate or something?
expected_answer_points: Contact the bank's hardship team before the due date; a temporary payment pause or reduced repayments may be possible depending on the circumstances
The bank may ask for supporting information such as a medical certificate or details of income and expenses, but should only ask for what is reasonably needed (verify)
Interest may still accrue during a pause, so ask how the arrangement affects the total owed and the loan term

questions.persona: Customer told their complaint will take longer
questions.question: Bank sent me a letter saying my complaint about a home loan error is 'complex' and they need more time past 30 days. Can they just keep extending it forever? At what point can I go to the ombudsman?
expected_answer_points: If the bank cannot give a final response within 30 calendar days, it must write explaining the reason for the delay and the customer's right to go to AFCA (ASIC RG 271)
The customer can lodge a complaint with AFCA once the timeframe has passed without a final response; they do not have to wait indefinitely
AFCA is free to use (afca.org.au, 1800 931 678)

questions.persona: Customer who got an SMS in the same thread as real bank messages
questions.question: Got a text saying 'Westpac: new payee added, if this wasn't you click link' and it showed up in the SAME message thread as my real Westpac texts. I clicked and put in my login. Oh no. What now??
expected_answer_points: Call the bank's fraud line immediately so it can secure the account; change the online banking password and check for unknown payees or transactions
Scammers can spoof sender IDs so fake texts appear in genuine message threads; the bank will not send links asking customers to log in or verify details (verify)
Report the scam to Scamwatch/ReportCyber and watch for follow-up calls pretending to be the bank

questions.persona: Customer whose card was used via digital wallet
questions.question: My physical card is in my wallet but someone added it to Apple Pay on another phone and spent like 1200 at JB Hi-Fi. How is that even possible and who pays for it?
expected_answer_points: Lock the card immediately and report the transactions to the bank; the bank will remove unknown digital wallet tokens and replace the card
Under the ePayments Code, customers are generally not liable for unauthorised transactions they did not contribute to; the bank investigates and refunds if confirmed (verify)
Never share one-time codes used to set up digital wallets; check whether any such code was received or shared

questions.question: Random $900 just landed in my account from someone I don't know. Can I keep it? Someone also messaged me on Facebook asking me to send it back to a different account.
expected_answer_points: Money paid by mistake is not the recipient's to keep; the bank may be asked to return it under mistaken payment rules (verify)
Do not send it on to a different account yourself, since this is a common scam/money-mule tactic; contact the bank and let it handle the return
Do not spend the funds while the bank investigates

questions.persona: Customer wanting call recordings for a dispute
questions.question: I want the recording of a phone call I had with your staff in March where they promised to waive a fee. Am I allowed to get it? How long do you keep call recordings?
expected_answer_points: Call recordings containing the customer's personal information can generally be requested as a privacy access request under the Privacy Act (APP 12) (verify)
The bank should respond within a reasonable period (generally 30 days); access may be refused only in limited cases, with reasons
Retention periods vary and the bank's privacy policy is the reference; make the request promptly (verify)

questions.persona: Identity theft victim with unknown credit enquiries
questions.question: My credit report shows 4 credit card applications I never made, at different lenders. I think someone stole my identity. How do I get these off and stop it happening again?
expected_answer_points: Ask the credit reporting bodies or the lenders that made the enquiries to correct the record; corrections are free
Request a ban period (credit freeze) with the credit reporting bodies to stop new credit being opened, initially for 21 days and extendable (verify)
Report the identity theft to police/ReportCyber and contact IDCARE for free support

questions.persona: Couple with joint and individual accounts across group brands
questions.question: Me and my wife have a joint account at Bank of Melbourne with 300k, plus I have 150k on my own at Westpac. How much of this is actually covered by the government guarantee?
expected_answer_points: The Financial Claims Scheme covers up to $250,000 per account holder per ADI; Bank of Melbourne is part of Westpac's banking licence so these balances are combined (verify)
A joint account is generally treated as split equally between holders, so each holder's share is added to their individual balances at the same ADI (verify)
Amounts above each person's $250,000 limit at that ADI are not covered; check fcs.apra.gov.au

questions.persona: Surviving spouse with joint account and no will
questions.question: my husband died without a will. we had a joint account and he had his own savings account too. can i still use the joint one? and how do i get his savings money without probate, its only about 20k
expected_answer_points: A joint account usually passes to the surviving account holder; notify the bank's deceased estates team with the death certificate
For a sole account without a will, the bank may release smaller balances without probate or letters of administration, depending on its threshold and an indemnity (verify threshold)
Larger estates may need letters of administration; suggest legal advice or the state Public Trustee for help

questions.persona: Customer seeking another person's account details
questions.question: My ex owes me money and I know he banks with Westpac. Can you tell me his account balance or freeze his account until he pays me back?
expected_answer_points: Refuse to disclose another person's account information or take action on their account; this is protected by privacy and confidentiality obligations
Suggest independent legal avenues for recovering a personal debt (e.g. community legal centre, local court) without giving case-specific legal advice
